reading.body:
H.R. 8241 has 29 Democratic cosponsors and no recorded lobbying filings naming it, so its support is entirely partisan and its pressure from industry is invisible in this data.

The bill is tagged to energy and data centers from its own text, which places it in the same legal territory as state and local rules on where AI compute may be built and who pays for its power. A bill that reaches data center power draws that connection directly, and the sponsor list shows it is a one-party vehicle so far.

What the data does not show is the bill's substance, its committee stage, or any vote. It records a sponsor, 28 cosponsors, a status date of 2026-04-09, and zero lobbying filings for 2025 or later. A filing that names a bill would show only that the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken, and here there are none to read either way.

summary: H.R. 8241, Power for the People Act of 2026. Latest status date 2026-04-09. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. 0 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
